q: we introduce EngramBench, a rigorous, capability-grounded benchmark governed by the strict axiom of capability overlap without solution overlap.
r: Include: new benchmark for coding agents on multi-hour development tasks, evaluating skill banks (context mechanism) on cost and time.

q: we propose RuleEvolve, a self-evolving framework for coding rules.
r: Include: evolves AGENTS.md-style coding rules for coding agents, measured on correctness, length and token cost (group b not narrowed by EC6).

q: we introduce TokenEconomizer, an external controller
r: Include: injects micro-skills and instructions into Claude Code, Codex and Copilot CLI and measures token cost over task sequences (group b).

q: We fix the agent scaffold (OpenCode), implement five compaction strategies inside it, and evaluate three frontier models on three long horizon benchmarks
r: Include: controlled comparison of compaction strategies and models, incl. ProgramBench build-from-scratch and loss of task rules; evaluation method contribution.

q: We study /retro, a skill that asks an agent to review a completed session and propose harness changes
r: Include: how Claude Code skills and context files (CLAUDE.md) change after retrospectives and whether they reduce repeated work (group b).
EC6: group (c) evaluation on SWE-bench Verified issue repair only, which is always excluded.

q: We present a longitudinal, cross-agent study of the instruction stacks captured in the first model requests of 1,886 releases
r: Include: studies the instructions and context that coding agents send to models, how they evolve and why (group b).

q: We construct CASE-Bench, a benchmark of 145 repository-level tasks from real CVEs in 51 projects.
r: EC6: group (c), security-focused benchmark of repository context for generated code, task is security rather than general code development.

q: We evaluate Claude Code with Haiku 4.5 against a raw-tool baseline on four repository-level tasks
r: EC6: group (c), tasks are fault localization, issue repair, test generation and security patching, none feature or project level.

q: we introduce Coding Agent Memory Gym II (CAMG-II), a suite of long-horizon agentic-RL environments spanning Shop, Coding, AutoResearch, General, and Visual.
r: IC1: RL memory distillation for general long-horizon agents (shop, research, visual); not SDD, context files or software development evaluation.
